Welcome to Ark Walworth
I'm proud to welcome you to Walworth Academy, where we seek to provide academic excellence and superb pastoral care for everyone in our school community. To that end, you'll find the team here at Walworth are dedicated to securing the best possible progress for students, placing our children at the heart of all decisions, and recognising their success.
The Walworth community is a thriving and exciting one in the heart of London. We are proud of the diversity of opportunity such a rich community offers both inside and outside of the classroom; and both in terms of academic pathways and enrichment opportunities. We seek to maximise this everyone in our Walworth Academy family of learners.
In taking up a place here at Walworth Academy, you will reap the benefits of:
At Walworth, our goal is for our students go on to be successful adults, empowered to take up their place in the world, and confident facing the challenges and opportunities that may bring. We look forward to welcoming the next generation of children who are excited and motivated by that prospect.
Jessica West
Our mission
At Ark Walworth Academy, we believe in the immense potential of each of our pupils and we are committed to giving them every possible opportunity to succeed. Every student should leave the academy with real choices: to continue into further and higher education or pursue the career of their choice. We have high expectations for pupil behaviour and achievement and equally high expectations for the quality of teaching in the classroom. This means a common commitment to creating a respectful and orderly environment where teachers can teach and students can learn. We recognise the need to support every child – academically, socially and emotionally. Through a combination of rigorous and engaging classes and a variety of learning experiences outside the classroom, our students can enjoy the full range of life's opportunities. Our academy is shaped by its culture of inclusion and mutual respect, which encourages a close working relationship between students and staff. We work hard every day to provide an inspirational and secure environment which recognises and celebrates success whilst challenging students to realise their full potential.
Our values
Our values underpin all our behaviour and interactions, and apply to all members of our academy family.
Sixth form welcome
Our provision for ages 16-18.
Culture and wellbeing

Upcoming open days - book a visit to see our school
Sixth form
Welcome to the Ark Walworth Academy Sixth Form!
Our key aim is for you to achieve the strong grades needed to progress to the next academic or vocational step of your career, as well as support you to become well-rounded, open minded, articulate and highly employable. We have high aspirations for all our students and have been delighted to see recent students achieve results that put us in the top 25% of schools and colleges nationally for the sixth form progress. This excellent achievement is driven by a core commitment to a high-quality learning experience in a formal and academic environment. Ofsted identifies that “…learning is always good and much is outstanding.”
The proportion of our students progressing to Russell Group universities exceeds national average, with 26% securing places at these institutions in 2019. Our recent leavers have gone on to excellent universities including Cambridge, King’s College, York and numerous other top tier institutions, as well as onto higher apprenticeships with prestigious employers including Balfour Beatty. In the last two years our students have also been awarded over £40,000 in Ark bursaries to support their continuing education.
We also provide a wide range of enrichment opportunities for you to gain broader experience and skills that will help you succeed at university and beyond in your professional working life.
By joining our sixth form you will have unique access to work experience and professional mentoring through our partnerships with law firms such as Shearman & Sterling and finance firms such as J.P. Morgan, Bloomberg, and State Street. Our dedicated pastoral provision, in conjunction with Art network partners, IntoUniversity and the Access Project, will ensure no barriers stand in the way of you reaching your desired destination.
We have a range of dedicated sixth form spaces around the school, including a fully equipped study centre with individual study stations and sixth form common room.
Our core expectation of students is that they are willing to embrace the hard work required to reach excellence in both their studies and extra-curricular activities. Our expectations are unashamedly high, both in terms of academic progress and attitude. High levels of attendance, impeccable punctuality and a professional dress code are at the core of our successful sixth form; we know that excellent habits support strong examination performance and build the right behaviours to be successful in the world of work.
We look forward to welcoming you to our Sixth Form community – don't hesitate to get in contact if you have any questions, or would like to arrange a visit.

Welcome to Drama
Intent statement
To introduce students to a range of theatre practitioners, to develop performance skills/techniques building each students confidence. To gain an understanding of a range of theatre performance styles and to introduce students to live theatre. To develop written/evaluation skills. To nurture a lifelong interest/ passion for theatre.
Head of Department
Ms Chapman
Drama Curriculum Coverage
Drama Curriculum Coverage (604.92 KB)

Implementation Key Principles:

Impact Key Principles
In evaluating the impact of our curriculum, we will consider:
The development of professionals into experts in their field through their work in supporting colleagues, supporting other schools, developing curriculum resource, becoming examiners etc.
Core Purpose
Students who choose to study drama develop skills in expressing themselves, further their creativity and become more assured performers. The history and changing styles of performance are a fascinating topic to study academically too. Drama is not all about the performance, there is so much more: history, politics, psychology, issues of justice and injustice, culture changes and our right to an identity are all central to what is covered.
Studying drama also helps students to develop important skills such as collaboration, analysis, communication and evaluation. These are skills that they need to use for the rest of their lives, in higher education and in work.
GCSE Drama guides students in how to have three perspectives when viewing a text or an idea: students consider and analyse from the points of view of a director, a designer and a performer. To understand this, students develop a knowledge of other times and cultures, including political, ideological and social changes in this country and across the world.
We aim to involve the largest possible number of students in productions: as performers, musicians, backstage or technical team members. In addition to our annual Shakespeare festival, we also team up with the Old Vic Theatre so that our senior students attend workshops where they can network with industry professionals and educate students in other schools. We also have a close working relationship with the Royal Court, Young Vic and Donmar Warehouse Theatres, benefiting from discount and free tickets plus workshops from industry professionals.
GCSE students are expected to form small theatre companies and run educational workshops for local primary schools.

Welcome to History
Intent statement
We want to provide a rigorous, diverse and transformational curriculum that develops a passion for the subject in our students and prepares them for success in school and beyond.​
Rigorous means that we want our historians to not only learn substantive knowledge but also the disciplinary knowledge. By this, we mean that students understand that there is not one history but histories and how ‘knowledge was established, its degree of certainty and how it continues to be revised by scholars, artists or professional practice’ (Counsell, 2018)’. ​
Diverse means that we want our historians to study a wide range of histories from differing time periods, places and contexts. Our curriculum covers periods from antiquity right up to the modern era and students study Asia, Africa, the Middle East, the Americas and Europe as they move through the school. We also want students to experience social, political, military, economic, and religious contexts of history.​
Transformational means that we aim to build a passion for the subject in our students so that they want to study the subject at university and beyond. Our students will also gain lifelong skills from the subject, such as the art of analysis, evaluation, and judgement that will serve them well in their futures.
Head of Department
Ms Elmi
